name: Pius X
role: Pope of the Catholic Church (1903–1914); canonised 1954
summary: Pope Pius X led the Catholic Church from 1903 to 1914 under the motto 'to restore all things in Christ': he condemned the French separation of Church and State, laicised schools and civil marriage laws, and in Pascendi (1907) and the anti-Modernist oath (1910) condemned the evolution of dogma and the democratisation of the Church.

sources.title: Vehementer Nos (encyclical on the French law of separation of Church and State, 11 February 1906), The Holy See
sources.author: Pope Pius X
sources.usedFor: His condemnation of separating Church and State, laicised schools, civil marriage laws and State control of the Church in France.

sources.title: Pascendi Dominici Gregis (encyclical on the doctrines of the Modernists, 8 September 1907), The Holy See
sources.author: Pope Pius X
sources.usedFor: His condemnation of Modernism: evolution of dogma, democratic forms in the Church, science independent of faith.

sources.title: E Supremi (first encyclical, 4 October 1903), The Holy See
sources.author: Pope Pius X
sources.usedFor: His programme 'to restore all things in Christ', religious instruction, and warning against rationalism.

sources.title: Il Fermo Proposito (encyclical on Catholic Action in Italy, 11 June 1905), The Holy See
sources.author: Pope Pius X
sources.usedFor: His view of the Church's civilising role and the proper relation of civil laws to the Gospel.

sources.title: Pius X, Pope St., New Catholic Encyclopedia (via encyclopedia.com)
sources.author: New Catholic Encyclopedia
sources.usedFor: Outline of his pontificate: the anti-Modernist campaign, France, Catholic Action.

sources.title: Notre Charge Apostolique (apostolic letter on Le Sillon, 25 August 1910), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius X
sources.usedFor: His condemnation of Le Sillon: authority comes from God, not the people; against levelling equality and the identification of the Church with democracy.

sources.title: Fin dalla prima nostra (motu proprio on Christian popular action, 18 December 1903), The Holy See (Italian text) with the TFP English translation
sources.author: Pope Pius X
sources.usedFor: His 'fundamental regulations' of Catholic social action: unequal elements of society, private property as natural right, duties of workers and masters, charity, Christian democracy distinct from social democracy.

sources.title: The Oath Against Modernism (Sacrorum antistitum, 1 September 1910), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Pope Pius X (motu proprio imposing the oath on clergy, confessors, preachers, superiors and seminary professors)
sources.usedFor: The oath he required of clergy rejecting the progress of dogma and exegesis by rationalist criticism.

sources.title: Lamentabili Sane Exitu (decree of the Holy Office condemning 65 Modernist propositions, 3 July 1907, issued on his decision), Papal Encyclicals Online
sources.author: Holy Office (by decision of Pope Pius X)
sources.usedFor: The condemnation of propositions on the evolution of dogma and critical exegesis.

notes: First audit. Positions are in his own encyclicals as pope (words; in-office statements of the Church's head, explicit enough for high where he states the thesis outright). His acts rest on the anti-Modernist oath and Lamentabili (texts at Papal Encyclicals Online), used only for reinterpret-religion; his words on the same point in Pascendi are a listed source. The 1903 motu proprio Fin dalla prima nostra was read in the Vatican's Italian text and the TFP English translation (a partisan site, checked against the Italian for the passages cited). Notre Charge Apostolique and the 1903 regulations (drawn from Leo XIII's Quod Apostolici Muneris, Rerum Novarum and Graves de Communi) give the economy, class and democracy answers. Read without a settled answer: Notre Charge on the Sillon's economic claims (he does not blame the goal of juster labour laws), Il Fermo Proposito on democracy and socialism (the encyclical has no passage on either), Vehementer Nos on the Concordat as a treaty (no matching statement), Pascendi on authority and the laity (internal Church governance). Many statements are modern and stay null.
